claims.text: Easy instances for human participants are also easy for language models.
Scaled-up and shaped-up models do not secure areas of low difficulty in which either the model does not err or human supervision can spot the errors.
Early language models frequently avoid user questions.
Scaled-up and shaped-up models tend to give an apparently sensible yet wrong answer much more often, including errors on difficult questions that human supervisors frequently overlook.
Stability to different natural phrasings of the same question is improved by scaling-up and shaping-up interventions.
Pockets of variability in response to natural question phrasings persist across difficulty levels in scaled-up and shaped-up models.

methodologies.name: Cross-family language model reliability evaluation
methodologies.description: Studying the relationship between difficulty concordance, task avoidance, and prompting stability across several language model families.
conditions: scaling-up (increasing size, data volume, and computational resources)

limitations.text: Scaled-up and shaped-up models fail to secure areas of low difficulty where the model does not err or human supervision can detect errors.
Scaled-up and shaped-up models produce plausible but wrong answers on difficult questions that human supervisors frequently overlook.
Pockets of instability to natural phrasing variations persist across difficulty levels despite scaling and shaping interventions.

future_work.text: A fundamental shift in the design and development of general-purpose artificial intelligence, particularly in high-stakes areas requiring a predictable distribution of errors.
